module

public import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Nth
public import Mathlib.NumberTheory.Divisors

@[expose] public section

/-!
# The increasing enumeration of the divisors of a natural number

Basic facts about `Nat.nth (· ∈ n.divisors)`, the increasing enumeration of the divisors of `n`.
-/

namespace Nat

/-- The smallest divisor of a positive number is `1`, i.e. the `0`th entry of the increasing
enumeration of its divisors. -/
lemma nth_divisors_zero {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : Nat.nth (· ∈ n.divisors) 0 = 1 := by
  rw [Nat.nth_zero]
  exact IsLeast.csInf_eq ⟨Nat.one_mem_divisors.mpr hn, fun y hy => Nat.pos_of_mem_divisors hy⟩

/-- Every divisor enumerated after index `0` is at least `2`. -/
lemma two_le_nth_divisors {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) {i : ℕ} (hi : i ≠ 0)
    (h : Nat.nth (· ∈ n.divisors) i ≠ 0) : 2 ≤ Nat.nth (· ∈ n.divisors) i := by
  have hfin : (Set.ofPred (· ∈ n.divisors)).Finite := n.divisors.finite_toSet
  have hpos : 1 ≤ Nat.nth (· ∈ n.divisors) i := Nat.pos_of_mem_divisors (Nat.nth_mem_of_ne_zero h)
  rcases hpos.lt_or_eq with h2 | h1
  · omega
  · exact absurd (Nat.nth_injOn hfin
      (Set.mem_Iio.mpr (Nat.lt_card_toFinset_of_nth_ne_zero h hfin))
      (Set.mem_Iio.mpr (Nat.lt_card_toFinset_of_nth_ne_zero
        (show Nat.nth (· ∈ n.divisors) 0 ≠ 0 by rw [nth_divisors_zero hn]; omega) hfin))
      (by rw [nth_divisors_zero hn]; omega)) hi

end Nat

reformulations.difference: Uses the hypothesis that the enumerated value is nonzero instead of explicitly bounding the index by n.divisors.card.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved in scratch.lean that Nat.nth (· ∈ n.divisors) i ≠ 0 ↔ i < n.divisors.card, for every n and i. Genuine divisors are positive, whereas out-of-range entries are zero. Also i ≠ 0 is equivalent to 0 < i, and the nonzero-output hypothesis already implies n ≠ 0. Thus the hypotheses identify exactly the genuine divisors after the first, including correct behavior for empty and singleton divisor sets.

reformulations.difference: The witness permits m = 0 and arbitrary k ≥ 1, rather than requiring positive m and k ≤ m.divisors.card.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every positive target n and each fixed m, proved that the Lean witness predicate is equivalent to m ≠ 0 together with a representation using 1 ≤ k ≤ m.divisors.card. When m = 0 every summand is zero. Otherwise replacing k by min k m.divisors.card preserves the sum and leaves a nonempty prefix, because all omitted entries are zero. Consequently the admissible m and their minimum agree on the intended positive domain. The zero fallback for nonexistent representations is explicitly supported by OEIS A167485. The extra input n = 0 does not affect the asymptotic questions.

reformulations.difference: Adds an existential density-one set A that does not occur in the limsup expression.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any proposition P, (∃ A : Set ℕ, A.HasDensity 1 ∧ P) ↔ P: the forward implication projects P, and the reverse takes A = Set.univ. Proved this both generically and for the exact limsup expression in use_site.lean. The statement therefore still asks whether limsup f(n)/n = ∞, without a density restriction.
